answer_text: - Physical activity: at least 30 minutes of regular activity for at least 5 days a week (150 minutes a week). NCD-3.1 Lifestyle counselling. Salt: a maximum of 1 teaspoon (5 g) of salt for the whole day, including salt in cooking; avoid pickles, papad and packaged salty snacks (NCD-3.1).

ANC-3.1 Hb cut-offs in pregnancy Anaemia Mukt Bharat (2026) uses these haemoglobin (Hb) cut-offs, in g/dL: Trimester No anaemia Mild Moderate Severe --- --- --- --- --- 1st and 3rd trimester 11.0 or more 10.0–10.9 7.0–9.9 below 7.0 2nd trimester 10.5 or more 9.5–10.4 7.0–9.4 below 7.0 Signs that suggest anaemia: pallor of the inner eyelids, tongue, palms and nails; tiredness; breathless (ANC-3.1).
Unconscious patient: refer immediately (call 108). Give nothing by mouth (ESC-6.3, ESC-1.3).
Mix 1 packet of ORS in 1 litre of clean drinking water (boiled and cooled), in a clean container. CHD-1.1 Preparing ORS. - Throw away ORS solution after 24 hours and make fresh. (CHD-1.1).

- After delivery: one Red IFA tablet daily for 180 days (up to 6 months after delivery). One Red IFA tablet daily for 180 days , starting from the second trimester of pregnancy. Each tablet contains 60 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid. ANC-2.2 IFA tablets (iron and folic acid) (ANC-2.2).
Child not able to drink or breastfeed: general danger sign, refer immediately to hospital (call 108/102) (ESC-5.1).
Pre-eclampsia danger signs in pregnancy: swelling of the face, severe headache, blurred vision. Refer immediately (call 102/108) (ESC-2.3).
This is outside my protocol book. Please ask the Medical Officer at the PHC (or your ANM). If any danger sign is present, refer immediately (SCP-1.2).

- Twice a day (total 1 g calcium per day ), starting from 14 weeks of pregnancy up to 6 months after delivery. Each tablet: 500 mg elemental calcium + 250 IU vitamin D3. ANC-2.3 Calcium tablets. Do not take calcium and IFA tablets together, because calcium reduces iron absorption. (ANC-2.3).

NUT-1.2 MUAC classification (children 6–59 months) Result MUAC Colour on the tape --- --- --- Severe acute malnutrition (SAM) below 11.5 cm , or oedema of both feet at any MUAC red Moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) 11.5–12.4 cm yellow No acute malnutrition 12.5 cm or more green SAM is also diagnosed by the ANM/MO when weight-for-height is below −3 SD. (NUT-1.2).
This is outside my protocol book. Please ask the Medical Officer at the PHC (or your ANM). If any danger sign is present, refer immediately (SCP-1.2).

MR-1 (measles-rubella) at 9 completed months to 12 months; can be given till 5 years of age. - fIPV-3 (third fractional IPV dose) at 9 months , given together with MR-1 (added to the schedule from 1 January 2023; children who received MR-1 by 31 December 2022 are not called again for fIPV-3) (IMM-2.3).

IMM-2.6 Minimum gaps between doses Vaccine Minimum gap between doses --- --- Penta, OPV, RVV 4 weeks PCV 2 months fIPV 8 weeks MR-1 to MR-2 (if delayed) 4 weeks OPV-3/Penta-3 to booster 6 months (IMM-2.6).

- Oedema check: press gently on the top of both feet; if a dent (pit) remains in both feet, the child has bilateral pitting oedema. Screen all children 6–59 months with the MUAC tape (mid-upper arm circumference) and look for bilateral pitting oedema (oedema of both feet) (NUT-1.1).

- Do not bathe the baby for the first 48 hours. Do not bathe a low birth weight baby until its weight is 2000 g; clean with a soft, warm, wet cloth instead.. - If the baby's temperature is below 97 °F, warm the baby by skin-to-skin contact and check again after about 1 hour; if it is still below 97 °F, refer (HBNC-2.2).

VIS-1.3 Counting conventions [block rule] Parameter Value --- --- upcoming_horizon_days 6 grace_days 28 followup_interval_days 30 td2_gap_days 28 vaccine_list_age_to_days 2554 hbnc_age_to_days 42 muac_age_from_days 184 muac_age_to_days 1824. - Children are on the vaccine part of the list while their age is 0 to 2554 days (under 7 years, the upper age for DPT boosters) (VIS-1.3).

ANC-1.2 Minimum four ANC check-ups Every pregnant woman should have at least four ANC check-ups. Check-up When --- --- 1st Within 12 weeks (as soon as pregnancy is suspected) 2nd Between 14 and 26 weeks 3rd Between 28 and 34 weeks 4th Between 36 weeks and term If a check-up is missed, bring the woman for her next check-up as soon as possible; do not wait for the next window. (ANC-1.2).
Fever lasting more than 7 days: danger sign, refer immediately for medical assessment (ESC-5.4).

ANC-1.3 PMSMA day (9th of every month) Under Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA), a check-up by a doctor/specialist is held at government health facilities on the 9th of every month , for women in the second or third trimester. Mobilise every pregnant woman in the second or third trimester to attend at least one PMSMA check-up (ANC-1.3).

IMM-2.2 At 6, 10 and 14 weeks Age Vaccines --- --- 6 weeks OPV-1, Penta-1, RVV-1, fIPV-1, PCV-1 10 weeks OPV-2, Penta-2, RVV-2 14 weeks OPV-3, Penta-3, RVV-3, fIPV-2, PCV-2. - Penta and RVV can be given till one year of age. - OPV can be given till 5 years of age (IMM-2.2).

A random blood sugar by glucostrip of 140 mg/dl or more is a suspected diabetes case → refer to the Medical Officer for confirmation. - Diagnosis is made by the MO: fasting 126 mg/dl or more , or 2-hour post-meal 200 mg/dl or more, or HbA1c 6.5% or more, or random 200 mg/dl or more with symptoms of diabetes. (NCD-1.3).
This is outside my protocol book. Please contact your block program management unit (BPMU) or supervisor (SCP-1.2).

IMM-2.1 At birth Vaccine When Upper limit --- --- --- BCG At birth or as early as possible till one year of age Hepatitis B birth dose (HepB-0) At birth within 24 hours of birth OPV-0 (oral polio, zero dose) At birth within the first 15 days (IMM-2.1).

- Vitamin A 1st dose (1 lakh IU, 1 ml) at 9 completed months with MR-1. - fIPV-3 (third fractional IPV dose) at 9 months , given together with MR-1 (added to the schedule from 1 January 2023; children who received MR-1 by 31 December 2022 are not called again for fIPV-3) (IMM-2.3).

ANC-2.5 Td vaccine in pregnancy Td-1 early in pregnancy, Td-2 4 weeks after Td-1 ; only one Td-Booster if she received 2 TT/Td doses in a pregnancy within the last 3 years. Full rule: IMM-4.1. (ANC-2.5).

- Chandrapuri is not a JE-endemic district , so JE vaccine is not given here.. MR-2 , DPT booster-1 (DPT-B1) , OPV booster (OPV-B) ; JE-2 only in endemic districts. - Vitamin A 2nd dose (2 lakh IU, 2 ml) at 16–18 months, then one dose every 6 months up to 5 years of age (9 doses in all) (IMM-2.4).
This is outside my protocol book. Please ask the Medical Officer at the PHC (or your ANM). If any danger sign is present, refer immediately (SCP-1.2).

At each visit ask about bleeding (how many pads changed in a day), fever, foul-smelling discharge, pain, breast problems, fits or abnormal talk. HBNC-3.1 Mother's check and supplements. - Continue one Red IFA tablet daily for 180 days after delivery and calcium (two tablets a day) up to 6 months after delivery (ANC-2.2, ANC-2.3) (HBNC-3.1).

Convulsions (fits / jhatke): general danger sign, refer immediately to hospital (call 108/102). Give nothing by mouth (ESC-5.1, ESC-1.3).

Start breastfeeding within 1 hour of birth. - Exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months : only breast milk — no water, honey, ghutti, animal milk or anything else. HBNC-2.1 Breastfeeding. - Feed on demand, day and night; give the first yellow milk (colostrum). (HBNC-2.1).

HBNC-1.1 HBNC visit schedule Place of delivery Number of home visits Visit days --- --- --- Institutional delivery 6 visits Days 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 and 42 Home delivery 7 visits Days 1, 3, 7, 14, 21, 28 and 42. - At every visit check both the baby (HBNC-1.3) and the mother (HBNC-3). (HBNC-1.1).
Baby birth weight under 1.8 kg: refer immediately to SNCU (call 102/108). Keep skin-to-skin (ESC-4.4).
Excessive vomiting in pregnancy: unable to take fluids, refer immediately to hospital (call 102/108) (ESC-2.6).
CHD-3.1 Counting breaths Count the child's breaths for one full minute when the child is calm (CHD-3.1).

ANC-5.3 JSSK free services Under Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK), pregnant women delivering in government facilities get free: delivery (including caesarean section), drugs, diagnostics, diet and blood; free transport from home to the health institution , between facilities in case of referral, and drop back home after 48 hours of stay (ANC-5.3).
Severe pallor with breathlessness in pregnancy: severe anaemia danger sign, refer immediately (call 102/108) (ESC-2.5).
Heavy postpartum bleeding (pad soaked in less than 5 minutes or more than 5 pads/day): refer immediately (call 108/102) (ESC-3.1).
Baby cold to touch (temperature below 95.9 F / 35.5 C): keep skin-to-skin and refer immediately (call 102/108) (ESC-4.3).
